title: Consecutive 5xx Wave Chronicle: Hosted API P0 Incident and Runbook Draft
body:
TL;DR: Between 2026-05-02 01:22 UTC and 2026-05-02 04:10 UTC the Hosted API experienced multiple short, high-amplitude waves of 5xx responses and streaming session failures affecting 18% of live requests at peak. The visible symptom was a chain of transient 5xx spikes that repeatedly recovered and returned over a 3-hour window. Impact: degraded latency and partial outages for streaming clients, elevated error rates for generation endpoints, and downstream client SDK retry amplification that prolonged the incident. Immediate mitigations restored baseline traffic within 40 minutes of the first escalation, but recurring waves required manual traffic shaping and adaptive throttles while a root-cause fix was deployed.

Incident severity and scope:
- Severity: P0 (production-wide customer-facing errors for hosted API)
- Affected surface: generation, streaming, and function-calling routes on hosted-api; primarily edge regions us-east1 and eu-west1
- Peak error rate: ~18% 5xx across API traffic, with streaming session failures measured at 12% of active sessions
- Time window: 2026-05-02 01:22 UTC to 2026-05-02 04:10 UTC
- Number of customers impacted (estimate): 120 orgs with medium-to-high traffic; a subset of enterprise tenants experienced persistent failures requiring SRE-assisted fallback

High-level timeline (synthesized from traces, logs, and on-call notes):
- 2026-05-02 01:16 UTC: Small uptick in tail latency detected by anomaly detector for hosted-api generation route (latency +95th percentile).
- 01:22 UTC: Pager fires (SRE primary) for 5xx error ratio crossing alert threshold (5xx_rate > 5% for 1 minute). Initial hypothesis: transient upstream dependency failure.
- 01:25–01:35 UTC: First wave of 5xx resolves after automatic edge retry and partial proxy restarts in us-east1. Error rate drops below alert threshold.
- 01:40 UTC: Second wave begins; distinct signature observed in streaming logs: session negotiation failures with TLS handshake timeouts followed by backend 503s.
- 01:45 UTC: Manual mitigation 1 applied: global short-term soft rate limit (10% reduction) and widened circuit-breaker windows for a subset of downstream proxies. Error rate dips but does not fully normalize.
- 02:10 UTC: Third wave with amplification pattern: client SDK retries cause request bursts, leading to KV lock contention in the auth/cache layer and subsequent queueing in the routing tier.
- 02:30 UTC: SREs enable tenant-scoped soft throttles and route heavy-callers to lower-priority capacity. Streaming fallback policy engaged for high-latency sessions.
- 03:05 UTC: Root cause narrow scope identified: combination of a rollback of proxy connection pooling defaults (deployed 2026-04-29) and an edge ratecap change that reduced available backend connections during short retry bursts.
- 03:25 UTC: Hotfix deployed reverting connection-pool timeout to previous stable value and increasing connection budget for streaming proxies; KV lock backoff tweaked.
- 03:50 UTC: Error rates stabilize and streaming sessions recover; monitoring shows regression windows close by 04:10 UTC.

Detection and monitoring notes:
- Primary alert: hosted-api.error_ratio.high (5xx ratio > 5% sustained) triggered from aggregate metrics.
- Secondary alerts: streaming.session_failures.rate, edge.tls.handshake.timeouts, proxy.conn_exhaustion.warn
- Observability gaps: no per-tenant 5xx SLI that would have flagged the disproportionate impact on a small number of heavy tenants earlier; trace sampling reduced during the time window which slowed root-cause triangulation.

Root cause (concise):
- A recent change to proxy connection pooling (rollback candidate deployed 2026-04-29) reduced idle connection recycling and lowered the effective connection budget under bursty retry patterns. In normal load this passed QA, but in real traffic combined with a concurrent edge ratecap tweak it created repeated transient connection exhaustion. The exhaustion cascaded into streaming handshake timeouts and upstream 503s. Client SDK retry behavior and aggressive global circuit breaker resets amplified the waves.

Contributing factors:
- Change to proxy connection pooling defaults not flagged as high blast-radius despite being infra-facing.
- Edge ratecap tweak reduced reserve capacity for short-lived reconnect bursts.
- No tenant-level 5xx SLI or automated per-tenant throttling prior to incident.
- Trace sampling was lowered in the region for cost reasons, reducing diagnostic signal.
- Client SDKs use linear retry with minimal jitter creating synchronized retry storms.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Applied short-term global soft rate limit (10% reduction) to reduce pressure on proxy layer.
- Widened circuit-breaker windows and increased connection recycling frequency for edge proxies in impacted regions.
- Engaged tenant-scoped soft throttles to isolate heavy noisy tenants and divert them to burst capacity.
- Enabled streaming fallback to non-KV-auth path for affected sessions where possible.
- Rolled back the proxy pooling change to the last stable config and increased connection budget for proxies.

Customer communication:
- Status page updated at 01:35 UTC and iteratively as mitigations applied.
- Customer success team notified high-impact enterprise tenants at 02:05 UTC with mitigation suggestions (short-term increase of client-side jitter and exponential backoff).
- Post-incident follow-up scheduled with top 10 affected customers for 2026-05-06.

Long-term corrective actions and owners (explicit owners and tentative ETA):
- Formalize change criteria for infra-facing proxy and edge defaults (owner: Marcus Li, ETA: 2026-05-16, JIRA: CHORE-592).
- Implement per-tenant 5xx SLI and alarms so noisy tenants are visible immediately (owner: Evelyn Romero, ETA: 2026-05-23, JIRA: SRE-1041).
- Add automatic tenant-scoped soft-throttling to routing tier (owner: Kai Nakamura, ETA: 2026-06-07, JIRA: ROUTE-317).
- Rework client SDK default retry algorithm to include jitter and exponential backoff guidelines (owner: devx-team, ETA: 2026-05-30, JIRA: DEVX-244).
- Restore higher trace sampling during burst-prone windows and instrument earlier failure modes in traces (owner: observability team, ETA: 2026-05-14, JIRA: OBS-610).
- Create a formal runbook for 'consecutive 5xx wave' incidents capturing detection, isolation, and controlled rollback steps (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-05-09, JIRA: RUNBOOK-88).

Runbook draft excerpt: (intended as an operational checklist for on-call)
1) Verify alert context and scope: query 5xx_rate by region, model, and tenant for last 10 minutes. If >5% globally and >10% in any region, escalate to P0.
2) If streaming sessions failing: check TLS handshake timeouts and proxied connection backlogs on edge proxies.
3) Apply temporary mitigations in this order:
   - a) Global soft rate limit (-10%) for 5 minutes, reassess.
   - b) Increase proxy connection recycling frequency and temporarily increase connection pool size in impacted region.
   - c) Enable tenant-scoped soft throttles for top noisy tenants identified by request volume in last 5 minutes.
   - d) Engage streaming fallback policy for affected sessions to a stateless handshake path.
4) If mitigations fail after 15 minutes, roll back any recent proxy/edge config changes deployed in the last 14 days; coordinate with infra-release owner.
5) When error rate is below 2% for 20 consecutive minutes, start gradual rollback of temporary throttles and document changes.

On-call forensic checklist and log queries (quick commands):
- Metrics: query hosted_api.5xx_rate{region=~"us.*|eu.*"}.rollup(1m)
- Traces: search for trace span containing 'handshake' or 'session_negotiation' and sort by duration
- Proxies: check proxy metrics proxy.connections.active, proxy.connections.idle, proxy.connection_errors
- KV/Auth layer: look for lock contention events kv.lock.wait_time > 50ms and retry counts
- Logs: grep for 'TLS handshake timeout' and '503 upstream' in last 60m

Post-incident retrospective notes (for the team discussion):
- We need clearer ownership for infra defaults that are allowed to be changed without explicit SRE signoff. This is the second time a pooling tweak had wider blast radius than expected.
- The incident exposed how client SDK behavior can materially affect server-side stability; deep coordination between devx and SRE is required.
- Quick wins: per-tenant throttles and an emergency rollback playbook would have shortened recovery time.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Why did the proxy pooling change behave differently under production TLS negotiation patterns vs staging? (ACTION: Marcus Li to reproduce by 2026-05-10)
- Can we implement a simulated retry storm test in platform CI to validate connection pool behavior under synchronous retries? (ACTION: platform-eng to prototype, ETA 2026-05-21)
- Should we add a pre-deploy checklist gate for infra-facing defaults that require SRE approval? (ACTION: SRE + infra-release to propose policy by 2026-05-09)

Action items (short list with owners and immediate due dates):
- Create RUNBOOK-88 draft and publish to Confluence (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-05-09)
- Open tenant 5xx SLI epic and start implementation planning (owner: Evelyn Romero, due: 2026-05-16)
- Revert and pin proxy pooling config in infra repo to stable (owner: Marcus Li, done: 2026-05-02)
- Customer follow-ups: schedule postmortems with top affected customers (owner: customer-success, due: 2026-05-06)

Appendix: On-call raw notes (verbatim snippets)
- 01:24 UTC: 'first spike recovered after proxy soft-restart, but saw TLS timeouts shortly after'
- 02:12 UTC: 'noticed repeated GET /session negotiate from same source with jitter 0 — likely SDK linear retry'
- 02:40 UTC: 'rolled back pooling config; connection metrics improved, KV wait_time dropped from 120ms to 18ms'

Status: draft for SRE review. Will incorporate test results from Marcus reproductions and the first customer follow-up before marking final.
